resources.string: Every photo you share can be scanned, matched and stored. FaceFlush scrambles faces before they leave your phone.
Everything happens on your phone. FaceFlush has no internet access, and the photos it saves contain no location or camera data.

Smears facial detail. Fools weaker AI, but in our tests a strong recognition model still matched about 3 in 4 heavily blurred faces. For real protection use Pixelate on Strong or Solid mask.

Bars across the eyes, nose and mouth, the parts face detectors rely on most. Leaves the rest of the face visible.

A trained pattern of tiny brightness changes that confuses recognition AI. Weak on its own; Max privacy below is much stronger. Medium leaves visible smudges on the face; Light looks almost untouched but protects much less. Not a guarantee: newer AI can learn to see through it.

resources.string: Max privacy needs at least one detected face.
Max privacy stopped before it finished.
Tap to review the photo, then save or share it.

Recognition AI turns a face into a list of numbers and compares those lists. FaceFlush makes tiny, trained brightness changes to the face (and optionally a small change in face shape) that push your numbers away from you. At low strength people barely see a difference; at the default strength the face looks slightly smudged.

Measured on 150 test faces, also after Instagram-style recompression. Max privacy is tuned on one AI; we also test a stronger AI it never saw, as a stand-in for unknown services:
• Quick cloak alone: the strong AI still recognised 99 in 100.
• Max privacy, strength 8 (barely visible): the tuned AI recognised fewer than 3 in 100, but the strong AI still recognised about 87 in 100.
• Max privacy, strength 16 (default, visible smudges): the strong AI recognised about 14 to 24 in 100.
• Max privacy, strength 24 (clearly visible): the strong AI recognised about 3 to 5 in 100.
This only covers the AI and photo changes we tested.

The face shape slider in More settings is off by default. In our tests it visibly changed faces while a strong AI still recognised 97 in 100 (88 in 100 at the maximum). It is kept only for people who want to experiment.
A similar tool (Fawkes, 2020) stopped working once newer AI came out. Assume any invisible protection will be beaten eventually, and that big companies use AI we cannot test against.
Max privacy takes about %1$d min per face and uses a lot of battery while it runs. Keep the phone charging if you can.
Use Pixelate on Strong or Solid mask. They were the only options that beat every AI we tested.
I understand this is not a guarantee
